summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose to ₹256 crore (from ~₹201 crore) with ~38% EBITDA margin, but Q4 revenue dipped as ~₹60 crore slipped into Q1 FY27.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated revenue of about ₹256 crore versus ~₹201 crore in FY25, EBITDA of about ₹97 crore (~38% margin) and PAT of about ₹79 crore (~31% margin). Order inflow of ₹1,075 crore was the highest in company history, with an order book of about ₹1,400 crore spanning dredging, charter hire and shipbuilding. Q4 margins were weak (~27% as stated by an analyst) because JNPA and Pondicherry contracts were single-payment on completion and their revenue (~₹60 crore) is expected in Q1 FY27. Management guided to ~30% revenue growth for FY27 and FY28 and a 35–40% EBITDA margin, and outlined a ₹400–500 crore FY27 capex plan.

financial_highlights.change: highest order win in company history
up sharply; JNPA short-tenure loan and other loans due in FY27

financial_highlights.value: No revenue recognised on JNPA and Pondicherry contracts in Q4
financial_highlights.change: Q4 EBITDA margin cited by analyst at ~27%; management says >40% when adjusting for project costs

segments.name: Dredging
segments.commentary: JNPA rock dredging (₹50 crore, 3-month scope) completed using River Pearl 47; DCI Paradip capital dredging (151,000 units, ₹15 crore) and Pondicherry port dredging completed. Management cites 35–40% EBITDA margin for dredging.

segments.name: Green Tugs / Chartering
segments.commentary: Two green tug contracts from VOC Port and Visakhapatnam Port worth ~₹650 crore with 15-year tenure; tugs to be built at Saphale yard, physical construction after monsoon, completion around mid-monsoon FY27.

segments.name: Shipbuilding (Knowledge Shipyard subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Executing IWAI orders for cutter suction dredgers and ancillary craft; management expects 20% revenue mix from shipbuilding this year. EBITDA margin 25–30% before government subsidy (10–15%), 35–40% including subsidy.

segments.name: Overseas (Bahrain, Myanmar)
segments.commentary: No operations in Bahrain (vessel redeployed to India) and no ongoing work in Myanmar (vessel moved to Ghogha, Gujarat); Bahrain had ~₹20 crore revenue with negative margin in the period discussed.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of ~30% YoY projected for each of FY27 and FY28.
EBITDA margin to stay within 35–40%; management said margins should not dip and there is a fair chance of 40–41% next year.
Q1 FY27 revenue expected above ₹100 crore with EBITDA margin above 40%, including ~₹60 crore carried over from Q4.
FY27 capex of ₹400–500 crore: close to ₹100 crore for shipyard, balance for dredgers and tugs; two dredgers and ~12,000 cubic metres of hopper capacity could be added in under 90 days.
Export shipbuilding orders expected from Q3 or Q4 FY27; yard designed for 14 vessels per year once fully functional.
capex_capacity: Saphale (Palghar) 15-acre shipyard land acquired near Vadhvan Port; yard to build vessels 10–120 m length, beam ~20 m, draft 5 m, focused on smaller vessels.
Shipyard development expected to take at least a year; capacity target of 14 vessels per year.
River Pearl 47 (India's largest and deepest self-propelled backhoe dredger) expected to be utilised over 240 days per year for next 2–3 years on rock dredging tenders at five ports.
Capital raise via preferential issue being deployed in phases over 12–16 months.
Shipyard subsidiary: KMEW holds 51%, to be raised to 75%; equity infusion in proportion to shareholding.
demand_pricing: Bid pipeline above ₹2,000 crore (domestic only) expected to convert over the next ~3 months; split about ₹950 crore dredging, ₹400 crore shipbuilding, ₹600 crore green tugs.
No international bids currently; international shipbuilding orders to be added in Q3–Q4 FY27, with marketing in Europe.
Fuel price rise offset by fuel pass-through clauses in all contracts; management reports no negative impact.
Bahrain sand mining project excluded from order book; vessels will not return until the situation normalises.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a slowdown in order booking, given only one ~₹50 crore DCI contract added since H1?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said there is no slowdown; bid pipeline exceeds ₹2,000 crore with orders expected over the next three months.

qa_highlights.question: Will tonnage tax apply to shipbuilding revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Tonnage tax applies only to vessel chartering and dredging; shipbuilding (Knowledge Shipyard) falls under corporate tax. Tonnage tax per management will not exceed 0.1% of chartering/dredging revenue; ~80% of FY27 revenue expected from dredging and chartering, 20% from shipbuilding.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margins drop to ~27% and revenue fall?
qa_highlights.answer: JNPA and Pondicherry contracts had costs in Q4 but single-payment billing on completion, so no Q4 revenue was recognised. ~₹60 crore moves to Q1; management says combined Q4+Q1 margin exceeds 40%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the ₹16 crore outstanding and debtor days above target?
qa_highlights.answer: The ₹16 crore relates to a Mangrol (Gujarat) dredging claim; two of three additional claims received, the third expected this FY. It is a one-off, not regular billing. Management aims to bring debtor days into the 45–60 day range.

qa_highlights.question: Why is short-term borrowing high alongside large fixed deposits?
qa_highlights.answer: Short-term debt is tied to the JNPA project and other short-tenure loans to be repaid in FY27 from accruals; the FD cash is earmarked for a specific vessel acquisition, so it is a conscious decision.

qa_highlights.question: What is the shipbuilding EBITDA margin and how does the subsidy work?
qa_highlights.answer: 25–30% before subsidy and 35–40% after; government subsidy of 10–15% applies per vessel, is set before construction, and decisions come within 60 days of application.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY27 capex of ₹400–500 crore be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash and debt first, equity only if needed depending on market conditions and vessel availability.

qa_highlights.question: Who owns the shipbuilding subsidiary and what is the capital structure?
qa_highlights.answer: KMEW holds 51% of the subsidiary, to be raised to 75%; remainder held by past owners and incoming shareholders.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 revenue recognition: ~₹60 crore carry-over must come through as stated; Q1 is seasonally weak due to monsoon.
Debtor days remain above the 45–60 day target; ₹16 crore Mangrol claim outstanding with one claim still under discussion.
Short-term borrowings (~₹114 crore) rising while holding large FDs; repayments due in FY27.
Overseas exposure: Bahrain and Myanmar currently idle; Bahrain revenue had negative margin.
Execution of shipyard and green tugs (9-month build post monsoon) and export orders expected in Q3–Q4 FY27; possible equity raise if debt/cash insufficient.
Management did not commit to quarterly revenue numbers; guidance is annual.
Tonnage tax benefit depends on fleet additions and segment mix.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on order wins, green tug and shipyard plans, and long-term growth targets. Becomes more defensive and vague when questioned on Q4 margin dip, debtor days, rising short-term debt and overseas revenue, attributing them to timing and one-off items.
key_quotes: So we are projecting a revenue increase of 30% year -on-year for the next 2 years.
So our EBITDA margins will continue to remain between 35% to 40%.
The revenue for these contracts, the last final bill for the Pondicherry contract and the JNPA contract will be recognized in quarter 1 of this year.

adds.what: Two dredgers plus ~12,000 cubic metres of hopper capacity (addable in under 90 days)
Saphale (Palghar) shipyard, target 14 vessels per year (land acquired, shipyard build takes at least a year)
Two green tugs for VOC Port and Visakhapatnam Port (~₹650 cr contracts, 15-year tenure), built at Saphale yard

growth.why: Management guides ~30% revenue growth for each of FY27 and FY28, backed by a ~₹1,400 cr order book, ₹1,075 cr FY26 order inflow, a ~₹2,000 cr bid pipeline, and ₹400–500 cr FY27 capex including two dredgers and ~12,000 cu m hopper capacity addable within 90 days, though the shipyard (14 vessels/yr) is a year-plus away and export orders are not yet in hand.
